issues.description: Sensitive payment card data (cardNumber, cvv) stored in plain interface without encryption or masking requirements. This violates PCI-DSS compliance standards.
issues.suggestion: Never store full card numbers or CVV in application code. Use a payment gateway (Stripe, PayPal) that handles PCI compliance. If necessary, only store tokenized references and last 4 digits.

issues.description: Credit card number passed as parameter and potentially logged. The chargeCard function receives full payment details including sensitive card data that could be exposed in logs or error messages.
issues.suggestion: Implement a proper payment gateway integration (e.g., Stripe, Square) where sensitive card data never touches your server. Use tokenization where the client-side sends tokens instead of raw card data.

issues.description: Card number validation only checks length === 16, but many valid cards have 13-19 digits (Amex has 15, Visa/MC have 16, etc.). This will reject valid cards.
issues.suggestion: Use the Luhn algorithm for proper card validation and support multiple card lengths: if (cardNumber.length < 13 || cardNumber.length > 19 || !luhnCheck(cardNumber)) { return false; }

issues.description: CVV validation allows both 3 and 4 digits, but doesn't validate that the card number is numeric or that CVV contains only digits.
issues.suggestion: Add validation to ensure numeric values: if (!/^\d+$/.test(cardNumber) || !/^\d{3,4}$/.test(cvv)) { return false; }

issues.description: Date expiry validation creates Date with 'new Date(2000 + parseInt(year), parseInt(month) - 1)' which will fail for years >= 2100 and doesn't handle current month correctly (card valid through end of month).
issues.suggestion: Fix year handling and check end of expiry month: const currentYear = new Date().getFullYear(); const fullYear = parseInt(year) + (parseInt(year) < 50 ? 2000 : 1900); const expiryDateObj = new Date(fullYear, parseInt(month), 0); // last day of month

issues.description: Payment error logged to console.error which may expose sensitive payment information in production logs. The error object might contain card details.
issues.suggestion: Remove sensitive data from error logging and use a proper logging service: logger.error('Payment processing failed', { userId, amount, lastFour, errorCode: error.code }); // Never log full error object

issues.description: No error handling or rollback mechanism if upgradeUserSubscription fails after charging the card. User could be charged without getting the subscription.
issues.suggestion: Implement proper transaction handling with rollback: try { const paymentId = await chargeCard(...); await upgradeUserSubscription(userId, tier, paymentId); } catch (error) { await refundPayment(paymentId); throw error; }

issues.description: hasFeatureAccess performs unsafe JSON.parse without try-catch. Corrupted data in database will crash the function.
issues.suggestion: Wrap JSON.parse in try-catch: try { const features = JSON.parse(subscription.features); return features.includes(feature); } catch { return false; }

issues.description: getUserSubscription performs unsafe JSON.parse without error handling. Malformed JSON in database will throw unhandled exception.
issues.suggestion: Add try-catch around JSON.parse: try { return { ...row, features: JSON.parse(row.features) }; } catch (error) { logger.error('Invalid subscription data', { userId }); return null; }

issues.description: Feature list duplicated inline as array literals. The 'unlimited_todos', 'priority_support', 'custom_themes' are repeated for both tiers, violating DRY principle.
issues.suggestion: Extract to constants: const BASE_FEATURES = ['unlimited_todos', 'priority_support', 'custom_themes']; const ENTERPRISE_FEATURES = [...BASE_FEATURES, 'api_access', 'team_collaboration']; const features = tier === 'premium' ? BASE_FEATURES : ENTERPRISE_FEATURES;

issues.description: Magic numbers for TAX_RATE (0.08) and PROCESSING_FEE (0.029) are hardcoded. Tax rates vary by jurisdiction and processing fees may change.
issues.suggestion: Move to configuration: const config = { TAX_RATE: process.env.TAX_RATE || 0.08, PROCESSING_FEE: 0.029 }; or accept as parameters for region-specific tax rates.

issues.description: Amount comparison uses '<' but doesn't account for floating-point precision issues. payment.amount of 10.999999 vs amount of 11.00 could cause unexpected behavior.
issues.suggestion: Use epsilon comparison for currency: const EPSILON = 0.01; if (payment.amount + EPSILON < amount) { throw new Error('Insufficient payment amount'); } or work in cents (integers).

issues.description: Database query returns 'rows' but doesn't specify return type. The db.query typing is unclear, making it harder to catch type errors.
issues.suggestion: Add proper typing: const result = await db.query<SubscriptionRow>(query, [userId]); if (result.rows.length === 0) { return false; }

testCoverage.summary: No test coverage exists for src/premium.ts. This file contains critical payment processing, subscription management, and feature access control logic handling financial transactions and security. All 7 functions (3 exported, 4 internal) are completely untested. Priority areas include: payment validation and processing (validatePaymentDetails, processPremiumPayment, chargeCard), pricing calculations (calculateSubscriptionPrice), subscription upgrades (upgradeUserSubscription), and access control (hasFeatureAccess, getUserSubscription). The file even contains warning comments acknowledging the lack of tests for this critical business logic.

suggestions.description: Extract feature list determination into a separate function to improve testability and reusability
suggestions.benefits: Makes feature lists testable in isolation, eliminates duplication of premium features in the ternary, and makes it easier to modify feature sets without touching subscription logic

suggestions.description: Replace early-return pattern with consolidated validation checks for better readability
suggestions.benefits: Reduces cyclomatic complexity from multiple early returns, groups related validations together, and makes it easier to understand all format requirements at once

suggestions.description: Extract expiry date validation logic into a separate function for better testability and reusability
suggestions.benefits: Isolates date parsing and comparison logic for unit testing, improves readability with a descriptive function name, and makes it easier to mock date comparisons in tests

suggestions.description: Extract subscription validity check into a reusable function to reduce duplication and improve consistency
suggestions.benefits: Creates a reusable validity check that can be used across multiple functions, improves testability by isolating date comparison logic, and makes the code more maintainable

suggestions.description: Use destructuring for database query results to improve readability
suggestions.benefits: More concise and modern syntax, clearer intent with array destructuring, and consistent pattern for handling single-result queries

suggestions.description: Extract pricing constants and calculation into a more flexible structure
suggestions.benefits: Separates price calculation logic from configuration, makes pricing formula more testable, and allows easier modification of rates without changing calculation logic

suggestions.description: Simplify date calculation for subscription validity using a more readable approach

refactorings.summary: The file contains critical payment and subscription logic that lacks test coverage. Key refactoring opportunities include: extracting feature list determination and expiry validation into testable functions (high impact), simplifying validation logic with consolidated checks (medium impact), and creating reusable mapping functions for database results (medium impact). These changes will improve testability, reduce duplication, and make the code more maintainable without altering behavior.
